questions.q: What is the passage mainly about?
options: Carnegie's steel empire and its rivalry with Standard Oil
The rise of kerosene and gasoline as household fuels
Rockefeller's oil empire and his later philanthropy
The Baptist church's role in building Cleveland's industry
questions.explain: It covers Standard Oil, its breakup, and Rockefeller's philanthropy.

questions.q: What business did Rockefeller concentrate his work on?
options: Railroad transport
Oil refining
Steel production
Commercial banking
questions.explain: He concentrated his business on oil refining.

questions.q: What did Rockefeller focus on during his retirement?
options: Philanthropy in education and medicine
Expanding Standard Oil's overseas operations
Running for national political office
Writing personal memoirs and fiction
questions.explain: In retirement he focused his energy and wealth on philanthropy, especially regarding education and medicine.

questions.q: How did the government respond to criticisms of Standard Oil in 1911?
options: The Supreme Court ordered the company dismantled
Congress imposed new protective tariffs on oil
State regulators took over day-to-day operations
The company was fined heavily but remained intact
questions.explain: The Supreme Court ruled in 1911 that Standard Oil must be dismantled for violation of federal antitrust laws.

questions.q: What does the passage suggest about Rockefeller's view of business?
options: Large trusts should be broken up for the public good
Competition among oil firms keeps business healthy
Large business growth reflects survival of the fittest
Charity work should be left to churches, not business
questions.explain: He was quoted as saying growth of a large business is merely survival of the fittest.
